notes.title: Never run broad --ignored cargo filters
notes.content: cargo test real_claude -- --ignored also matched paid real-model tests and spent tokens without asking. Run ignored real tests only by their exact full name with --exact; list them first with -- --ignored --list.

notes.title: Ask before spending tokens
notes.content: The user wants to be told before real models are run: say what it costs first and wait for the go. Report any accidental spend at once.

notes.title: Measure before saying optimized
notes.content: Never call something optimized without numbers. Required prompt text such as rules, protocols and the grants no permissions notices is not shortened as an optimization.

notes.title: RTK was removed
notes.content: Phase 3 (RTK) was built and then removed (ADR 0023): no Atlas agent runs commands through Atlas, so it saved nothing. Atlas never installs software or edits ~/.claude.

notes.title: Commits: conventional, in the user's name, only own files
notes.content: Use conventional commits in the user's name with no Claude co-author trailer, and commit only the files that belong to the work, never the user's unrelated changes (docs/guia and RESUMO.md were theirs).

notes.title: Optimization flags defaults
notes.content: metrics and guardrailsEnabled are on by default; contextEnabled and skillsEnabled are off because they change prompts.

notes.title: Inspect Claude's tools at zero cost
notes.content: claude -p ... --model not-a-real-model-xyz prints its init message (tools, mcp_servers, skills) and fails at the first request, so it costs nothing.

notes.title: --tools does not limit MCP tools
notes.content: For Claude, --tools does not limit MCP tools; --disallowedTools mcp__srv__tool does (fail-open for new tools). A bad tool schema drops all the server's tools yet the server shows connected. text_only must get no --mcp-config.

notes.title: Figma MCP is HTTP with OAuth
notes.content: The official Figma MCP is HTTP+OAuth, not stdio, so it waits for an HTTP transport. Chrome DevTools MCP is stdio via npx: pin the version and never auto-start it.

notes.title: A slow npx start looks like a failed MCP server
notes.content: A slow npx start was reported as a failed MCP server until MCP_TIMEOUT was set. The nvm, fnm and volta PATH must be found for node and npx (the user uses nvm).

notes.title: MCP secret variables can collide
notes.content: Secret variable names collided between servers named web-2 and web_2; the names are normalised before they reach the environment.

notes.title: MCP works differently on each runtime
notes.content: Claude needs --allowedTools; Codex needs default_tools_approval_mode=approve; OpenCode takes an allow-list through the tools map and has no tool filter, so named grants are refused; Antigravity is not strict.

notes.title: Name the MCP servers in the prompt
notes.content: Codex ignored the browser server until the prompt named it: the workflow setting executionPolicy.announceIntegrations (default on) adds two lines naming the granted servers.

notes.title: MCP search uses the official registry
notes.content: mcpservers.org has no public API (robots disallow /api, 403), so the official registry registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers is used through the system curl.

notes.title: Never overwrite a CLI MCP config
notes.content: Writing to a CLI config keeps a .atlas-backup copy, never overwrites, and refuses files it cannot parse (JSON with comments). Secrets are only written as env references.

notes.title: Template text must not ask for a test run
notes.content: No Atlas agent can run commands: the editing prompt says so and Claude gets only Read, Grep, Glob, Edit and Write. A workflow template must never ask for a test run or claim one.

notes.title: Import is preview first
notes.content: Config import is parse, then a preview that changes nothing, then a decision per item (create, use existing, replace, skip), then one atomic modify. Agents arrive read-only unless the person ticks keep permissions; matching is by name only.

notes.title: What the export leaves out
notes.content: Not exported on purpose: workspaces, MCP connections, grants and secrets, conversations, runs, usage, rules, harness. A model or runtime missing on the destination is reported with alternatives, never swapped silently.

notes.title: The phone may only narrow authority
notes.content: The phone can deny, never allow; guardrail approvals, command approvals and apply code are desktop-only. Any new remote action is a line in policy.rs plus a route plus a test, never a generic proxy of Tauri commands.

notes.title: Mobile access is HTTP only
notes.content: No HTTPS or push, on purpose. Pairing is single-use and the session is HttpOnly with Host and Origin checks. The server is off at start.

notes.title: Atomic writes must not follow symlinks
notes.content: Use infrastructure/atomic_file.rs: the temp file is created with create_new, fsync, and keeps the permissions. Hand-rolled writes followed symlinks at the temp name. FsRuntimeConfigFiles refuses links: a planted .mcp.json could copy private files into a repo.

notes.title: Use LockExt for mutex locks
notes.content: Use LockExt (lock_or_recover) everywhere instead of unwrap on a Mutex, so a poisoned lock does not take the app down.

notes.title: Logging is eprintln
notes.content: Logging is eprintln!, invisible in a release GUI build; there is no tracing crate. Pending: cargo audit is not installed, so the Rust dependencies are unaudited.

notes.title: live_workspace timing tests fail under load
notes.content: The live_workspace timing tests fail only under CPU contention (two cargo runs at once) and pass alone. Rerun alone before investigating.

notes.title: The Claude CLI may be logged out
notes.content: When the Claude OAuth expires only the runtime unavailable path is proven. Check claude auth status before a real Claude run; only the user can log in.

notes.title: Tests drift when the agent selection changes
notes.content: After commit 9901d80 three tests were stale on main and CI was red; they were updated to the intended behavior. Check the contract tests when the selection of agent or model changes.

notes.title: One retry for a missing result block
notes.content: A step whose model forgets the result block gets one protocol retry (MAX_PROTOCOL_RETRIES=1, StepCompletion::NoValidOutcome); quick templates fail on a judge's rejection (verdict_gate).

notes.title: Agents without a contract invalidate templates
notes.content: Agents created without a result contract make 5 of 8 templates invalid; the UI always sends one.

notes.title: Apply serialises integration decisions
notes.content: Checkout changes during a run are listed and hold the first Apply; integration decisions are serialised. A run is announced completed only after its integration settled.

notes.title: Codex's seatbelt fails inside ours
notes.content: Codex's own seatbelt fails inside Atlas's sandbox-exec (sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted), so adapt_to_confinement swaps --sandbox to danger-full-access and keeps read-only runs read-only through the profile.

notes.title: Observe sandbox writes with find -newer
notes.content: sandbox-exec's (trace) and the system log are not usable for discovery; observe writes with find -newer. Network by domain is impossible in SBPL.

notes.title: SBPL regex needs a single backslash
notes.content: In sandbox profiles a regex needs a single backslash (\.) and parameters go only through -D.

notes.title: A worktree commit writes to the main .git
notes.content: A git worktree commit writes to the MAIN repo .git: it needs worktrees/<id>, objects, refs/heads/atlas and logs/refs/heads/atlas. hooks, config and main stay protected.

notes.title: Memory notes are untrusted
notes.content: Notes go into the prompt under a notice as hints, never instructions; they grant no permission. Auto never applies to preference notes or the User scope; an automatic note is held until an independent validator passes the run.

notes.title: Small models ignore the memory block
notes.content: Claude haiku never wrote the atlas-memory block (0 of 18 runs); the rule goes at the end of the prompt, after the task. Success of a step is not the truth of a lesson.

notes.title: cargo fmt reformats unrelated files
notes.content: cargo fmt also reformats two pre-existing unformatted files (commands/harness.rs and infrastructure/harness_store.rs); that diff is not part of the work.

notes.title: Another session may use the same tree
notes.content: When another Claude session works in the same tree, never touch or format its files and never git add -A; commit with selective staging. Cargo runs from two sessions at once make timing tests fail.

notes.title: Stitch gives timeouts but finishes
notes.content: edit_screens and generate_screen_from_text time out but the generation ends: do not resend, wait for the user to confirm the screen and check with list_screens.

notes.title: Modelos do Copilot vêm do ACP
notes.content: Os modelos do Copilot vêm do ACP (copilot --acp, session/new), nunca de help config: ele lista 28 que a conta não tem. A conta do usuário só aceita auto.

notes.title: Mac lento: espere, não mate processos
notes.content: Se o Mac estiver lento (syspolicyd alto), espere em vez de matar processos: outras sessões podem ter testes rodando no mesmo target/.

notes.title: Prompts do Stitch: uma tela por vez
notes.content: Ao enviar prompts ao Stitch, use o P0 mais o bloco TELA, mostre os prompts ao usuário antes de enviar, mande uma tela por vez e registre em prompts.md.

notes.title: O Stitch inventa funções
notes.content: O Stitch inventa moldura e funções (busca ⌘K, Sync OK, Exportar log). O P0 v2 proíbe; o que sobrar vai para a lista do que o Stitch mostra e o app não tem. O Stitch é referência visual, nunca especificação funcional.

notes.title: Interface com informação demais
notes.content: O usuário acha que o Atlas mostra informação demais e quer separar melhor, mantendo o tema. Use os componentes compartilhados Badge, CollapsibleSection, OverflowMenu e Steps.

notes.title: Rich Presence desligado por padrão
notes.content: O Discord Rich Presence vem desligado; showNames separa nomes de textos genéricos. Não foi testado contra um Discord real e o Windows (named pipe) não foi testado.

notes.title: Sandbox: só a escrita é restrita
notes.content: O sandbox do macOS permite tudo por padrão e nega apenas a escrita fora do worktree e do tmp da execução; a leitura de credenciais (.ssh, .aws) é negada. A rede por domínio é impossível no SBPL.

notes.title: Dossiê de design por módulo
notes.content: A repaginação visual é feita por módulo em docs/design-review/<módulo>/ com README, prompts.md e plano-implementacao.md; o processo fica em docs/design-review/_comum/.
